chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man upon whom is the freeing of a slave, and he wished to free a person: which of the two is better, that he free an elderly old man or a beardless youth? He said: “Free the one who is more self-sufficient. The elderly old man is better than the beardless youth.”

key_terms.أَغْنَى نَفْسَهُ: more self-sufficient and able to manage his own affairs
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: the obligation of freeing a slave
key_terms.نَسَمَةً: a human soul/person to be emancipated

ai.seo_question: When fulfilling the obligation of freeing a slave, is it better to emancipate an old man or a young man?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal preference in fulfilling the obligation of emancipating a slave. It indicates that when choosing whom to free, preference is given to the one more able to manage independently, and it states that an elderly man is better than a young beardless man in this context.
